note: BTK inhibitors controlled nephritis and autoantibodies in NZB/W lupus mice at a stated occupancy, but fenebrutinib, evobrutinib and elsubrutinib all missed their SLE primary endpoints.
label: SLE (BTK)

engagement.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active SLE on standard therapy)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read (PMC5374071). G-744 is a Genentech sibling of fenebrutinib; opening year is its publication, which coincides with the first member SLE trial start (NCT02908100, Jan 2017).
engagement.judgement: G-744 is not a member, so product_in_model false; evobrutinib (Haselmayer 2019) and ABBV-105 (Goess 2018) later ran the same strain.
engagement.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
engagement.note: G-744, a Genentech sibling of fenebrutinib, ablated plasmablasts and lowered autoantibodies in NZB/W lupus mice; opens the fenebrutinib track.
engagement.quote: Selective Btk inhibition ablated plasmablast generation, reduced autoantibodies, and - similar to cyclophosphamide - improved renal pathology in IFNα-accelerated lupus.

engagement.magnitude_basis: plasmablast RNA signature and anti-dsDNA change vs placebo (mouse: ablated/reduced)
engagement.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active SLE on standard therapy)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read; full text paywalled. Year from the ACR/ARP 2019 abstract (first published 2019-10-23), which reported reduced anti-dsDNA, IgG and the plasmablast RNA signature; rule 6 earliest public date.
engagement.judgement: Paired: the trial does not set its biomarkers beside the mouse data in the abstract. Plasmablast signature and autoantibodies are downstream of BTK.
engagement.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
engagement.note: Fenebrutinib lowered the plasmablast signature and anti-dsDNA in SLE patients, as G-744 had in NZB/W mice; first public in the ACR 2019 abstract (23 Oct 2019).
engagement.quote: By week 48, patients treated with fenebrutinib had reduced levels of a BTK-dependent plasmablast RNA signature, anti-double-stranded DNA autoantibodies, total IgG, and IgM, as well as increased complement C4 levels, all relative to placebo.

engagement.magnitude_basis: anti-dsDNA, complement and Ig change at week 52 (mouse: autoantibodies and plasma cells reduced)
engagement.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy)
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9837396); Haselmayer 2019 abstract only. Anti-dsDNA reported as status change, quantitative values in a supplement not read.
engagement.judgement: Evobrutinib's own NZB/W data (Haselmayer 2019) predicted autoantibody reduction; in patients it did not move. Scored on the evobrutinib track only; fenebrutinib's same is its own track.
engagement.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
engagement.note: Evobrutinib lowered autoantibodies in lupus mice but left anti-dsDNA, complement and IgG unchanged in SLE patients.
engagement.quote: However, there were no clinically meaningful changes in serum IgG, IgM, or IgA or in anti‐dsDNA antibodies or complement levels observed, and no opportunistic infections (≥grade 3) were recorded in the evobrutinib treatment arms.

engagement.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read (PMID 30988116). Published after the evobrutinib SLE trial began (Jan 2017); the occupancy work likely predated it.
engagement.model: Mouse BTK-occupancy PK/PD (blood occupancy vs lupus disease score)
engagement.note: Mouse PK/PD linked about 80% blood-cell BTK occupancy by evobrutinib to near-complete lupus disease inhibition.
engagement.quote: Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling showed that mean BTK occupancy in blood cells of 80% was linked to near-complete disease inhibition in both RA and SLE mouse models.

engagement.magnitude_basis: BTK occupancy in healthy volunteers (full at 25 mg/day) vs 80% mouse target
engagement.population: Healthy volunteers (evobrutinib phase I, multiple ascending dose)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read (Becker 2019, PMID 31654487, epub 2019-11-29). Wallace 2022 later reported high occupancy in SLE patients too (values in a supplement not read).
engagement.judgement: Healthy volunteers count for engagement; rule 6 earliest public date. Retrodiction: human BTK inhibition in blood (fenebrutinib healthy volunteers, Herman 2018, epub 2018-03-23) was public before this mouse occupancy model (2019-04-15).
engagement.model: Mouse BTK-occupancy PK/PD (blood occupancy vs lupus disease score)
engagement.note: Evobrutinib reached full blood BTK occupancy in healthy volunteers, as the mouse readout required; human BTK blockade was already public (fenebrutinib, 2018), so retrodiction.
engagement.short: HV: full BTK occupancy at 25 mg
engagement.quote: After multiple dosing, full BTK occupancy was achieved with 25 mg, indicating slow turnover of BTK protein in vivo.

engagement.model: Human PK/PD model of BTK inhibition fitted to fenebrutinib healthy-volunteer data
engagement.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active SLE on standard therapy)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read (Herman 2018, epub 2018-03-23). The SLE trial (NCT02908100) chose its regimens from this model before its publication.
engagement.judgement: Opening at the model's publication; it was fitted to healthy volunteers, so its first test in the context is SLE patients.
engagement.note: PK/PD simulations on healthy-volunteer data set fenebrutinib regimens expected to keep BTK inhibition high over the dosing interval.
engagement.quote: Based on pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations, a once-daily dosing regimen (e.g., 100 mg, q.d.) is expected to maintain a high level of BTK inhibition over the dosing interval.

engagement.model: Human PK/PD model of BTK inhibition fitted to fenebrutinib healthy-volunteer data

engagement.quote: These concentrations were associated with reductions in pBTK levels consistent with those predicted based on pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling using healthy volunteer data
engagement.note: In SLE patients, fenebrutinib troughs lowered pBTK as the healthy-volunteer PK/PD model predicted; sustained to week 48.
engagement.judgement: pBTK (BTK autophosphorylation in PBMC lysate) taken as a direct readout of target inhibition; the paper states the model-patient agreement itself.

dose.judgement: Healthy-volunteer PK counts; rule 6 earliest public date. Target reached, so dose same; the SLE failure is efficacy only. Evobrutinib's own human occupancy came after the mouse model, so prospective.
dose.model: Mouse BTK-occupancy PK/PD (blood occupancy vs lupus disease score)
dose.note: Healthy volunteers reached full BTK occupancy at 25 mg/day, above the mouse 80% target; SLE patients later did too, yet the trial failed.
dose.quote: After multiple dosing, full BTK occupancy was achieved with 25 mg, indicating slow turnover of BTK protein in vivo.

efficacy.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active SLE on standard therapy)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read. Opening year is Katewa 2017 publication and the first member SLE trial start (Jan 2017).
efficacy.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
efficacy.note: G-744, a Genentech sibling of fenebrutinib, improved lupus nephritis in NZB/W mice, outperforming BAFF and Syk blockade.
efficacy.quote: G-744 is efficacious, and superior to blocking BAFF and Syk, in ameliorating severe lupus nephritis in both spontaneous and IFNα-accelerated lupus in NZB/W_F1 mice in therapeutic regimens.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: SRI-4 at week 48: 51-52% vs 44% placebo, NS (mouse: disease ameliorated)
efficacy.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active SLE on standard therapy)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read (Isenberg). Wallace 2022 (full text) states the comparison for the class: 'Several studies have demonstrated that BTK inhibitors are effective in murine models of SLE; this effectiveness, however, has not translated to phase II clinical trials of SLE'. Evobrutinib (Haselmayer 2019) and ABBV-105 (Goess 2018) had their own NZB/W efficacy.
efficacy.judgement: Year set by the ACR/ARP 2019 abstract (first published 2019-10-23), earlier than the registry results (2020-07-07); rule 6. Model side is G-744 (sibling). Evobrutinib and elsubrutinib are scored on their own tracks (appended entries).
efficacy.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
efficacy.note: Fenebrutinib missed SRI-4 in SLE (51-52% vs 44%) despite pathway inhibition, against efficacy in lupus mice; first public in the ACR 2019 abstract.
efficacy.quote: While fenebrutinib had an acceptable safety profile, the primary end point, SRI-4 response, was not met despite evidence of strong pathway inhibition.

efficacy.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
efficacy.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read (PMID 30988116, epub 2019-04-15); full text (PMC6500888) per checker: IFN-a-accelerated NZB/W F1 mice.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the evobrutinib track on the NZB/W mouse; evobrutinib itself was dosed.
efficacy.note: Evobrutinib reduced disease severity and histological damage in NZB/W lupus mice before any member SLE result.
efficacy.quote: In mouse models of RA and SLE, orally administered evobrutinib displayed robust efficacy, as demonstrated by reduction of disease severity and histological damage.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: SRI-4 at week 52 and SRI-6 in high disease activity, no difference vs placebo (mouse: robust efficacy)
efficacy.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
efficacy.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy)
efficacy.confidence_note: Wallace 2022 full text (PMC9837396) and the ACR Convergence 2020 abstract (presented 2020-11-07) read; year from the ACR abstract, before the registry results (2020-12-17).
efficacy.judgement: Co-primary endpoints, both missed, so the authors call the trial a failure: contra on the evobrutinib track.
efficacy.note: Co-primary design: SRI-4 at week 52 (all) and SRI-6 (high disease activity) both missed at every evobrutinib dose, against efficacy in lupus mice.
efficacy.quote: This phase II, dose-ranging trial in SLE failed to show a treatment effect of evobrutinib versus placebo at any dose.

efficacy.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read (Goess, PMID 29862859, epub 2018-07-23); ABBV-105 is elsubrutinib.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the elsubrutinib track on the IFN-a-accelerated NZB/W lupus nephritis model; elsubrutinib itself was dosed.
efficacy.note: ABBV-105 (elsubrutinib) reduced disease in IFNα-accelerated NZB/W lupus nephritis, with BTK occupancy tracking efficacy.
efficacy.quote: ABBV-105, a selective BTK inhibitor, demonstrates compelling efficacy in pre-clinical mechanistic models of antibody production and in models of rheumatoid arthritis and lupus.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: SRI-4 with glucocorticoid <=10 mg at week 24; arm stopped for lack of efficacy (mouse: disease reduced)
efficacy.model: NZB/W F1 lupus mice (spontaneous or IFNα-accelerated nephritis)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read (Merrill 2024, PMID 38923871, epub 2024-08-07); year from the registry results posting (2023-07-21); no earlier congress report found.
efficacy.judgement: Elsubrutinib monotherapy arm stopped at a planned interim for lack of efficacy: contra. The elsubrutinib + upadacitinib arm (ABBV-599 high dose) also missed its primary (48.5% vs 37.3%, P = 0.081): same status, kept in note.
efficacy.note: Elsubrutinib alone stopped for lack of efficacy in SLEek; combined with upadacitinib (ABBV-599 high dose) it missed the primary too (48.5% vs 37.3%, P = 0.081).
efficacy.quote: The ABBV-599 low dose and elsubrutinib arms were discontinued after a planned interim analysis showed lack of efficacy (no safety concerns).

patient_trials.quote: More patients achieved the primary endpoint with upadacitinib (54.8%; P = 0.028) and ABBV-599 high dose (48.5%; P = 0.081) versus placebo (37.3%).

safety.population: Unselected (moderately to severely active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy)
safety.confidence_note: No member is approved, so no FDA review package exists; GLP toxicology for fenebrutinib, evobrutinib and elsubrutinib is not public.
safety.judgement: Evobrutinib's liver-enzyme excess in SLE could be a missed or predicted harm; without the toxicology the comparison cannot be made.
safety.model: Nonclinical GLP toxicology of member drugs (species not public)
safety.note: Toxicology unpublished for all three members; evobrutinib raised liver AESIs in SLE (7.7% vs 2.6%), but no model prediction is public to compare.
safety.short: Tox unpublished; liver signal in SLE
safety.quote: Liver‐related AESIs were proportionally higher for evobrutinib‐treated patients (pooled evobrutinib, n = 27, 7.7%) than for placebo patients (n = 3, 2.6%).
